page: Microsoft Azure E64as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor using the x86_64 architecture, providing 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled at up to 3.7 GHz. The hardware profile includes 512.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. Local storage is not included on this instance, necessitating remote storage configurations such as Azure Premium Storage. Hardware accelerators such as dedicated GPUs are absent.

In benchmark evaluations, the E64as_v5 demonstrates high-throughput parallel compute and memory subsystems. PassMark memory testing places the instance in the top 10% with a score of 2982.1, reinforced by cached memory read bandwidth reaching 4165.53 GB/sec. Multithreaded execution is robust, achieving top 25% results across stress-ng multi-core (86370.39), Geekbench multi-core (17574.0), and PassMark CPU (62416.81). It also demonstrates high transactional capacity, delivering 63.15 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 25630.44 in PassMark database operations. Conversely, single-core metrics register in the middle 50%, and CPU-based LLM text generation drops to 2.47 tokens per second on a 70B model.

The resource distribution favors workloads requiring massive memory capacities coupled with dense multithreaded computation. Because the instance lacks local ephemeral NVMe storage, input and output performance relies on attached storage networking, requiring balanced architectural planning for data persistence. The instance delivers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, in-memory caching layers such as Redis, large relational databases, and multi-threaded compilation pipelines without incurring the expense of GPU hardware.
description: Microsoft Azure E64as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine equipped with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 512.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at up to 3.7 GHz across 32 physical cores. Featuring an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the system delivers high memory subsystem performance, ranking in the top 10% in PassMark memory testing and processing 63.15 million Redis SET operations per second. Multithreaded benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core rank in the top 25%, while single-thread execution falls within the middle 50%. The instance contains no bundled local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on remote storage volumes. This hardware footprint provides strong cost-performance tradeoffs for memory-intensive applications, in-memory databases, large-scale data processing, and enterprise application servers requiring substantial RAM allocations without the overhead of specialized GPU accelerators.
